claim: Glaucoma is a leading cause of irreversible blindness.
source: Glaucoma is a leading cause of irreversible blindness.
evidence: This is a statement of established medical knowledge about glaucoma's impact on vision.

claim: TMSC transplantation significantly increased the TM cellularity.

claim: TMSC transplantation promoted myocilin secretion from TM cells into the aqueous humor to reduce endoplasmic reticulum stress.

claim: TMSC transplantation repaired the TM tissue with extracellular matrix modulation.

claim: Primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) is the most common type of glaucoma with a prevalence of 0.5–7.0% in adults.
source: Primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG), the most common type of glaucoma with a prevalence of 0.5–7.0% in adults, can result in damage of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) and irreversible vision loss (Broman et al., 2008; Quigley, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: POAG can result in damage of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) and irreversible vision loss.
source: Primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG), the most common type of glaucoma with a prevalence of 0.5–7.0% in adults, can result in damage of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) and irreversible vision loss (Broman et al., 2008; Quigley, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The progression of POAG has been demonstrated to be correlated with elevated intraocular pressure (IOP).
source: The progression of POAG has been demonstrated to be correlated with elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) (Heijl et al., 2002)

claim: Elevated IOP is associated with reduced trabecular meshwork (TM) cellularity.
source: The progression of POAG has been demonstrated to be correlated with elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) (Heijl et al., 2002), which is associated with reduced trabecular meshwork (TM) cellularity (Alvarado et al., 1984; Alvarado et al., 1981)
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Elevated IOP is associated with malfunction of TM phagocytosis.
source: The progression of POAG has been demonstrated to be correlated with elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) (Heijl et al., 2002), which is associated with reduced trabecular meshwork (TM) cellularity (Alvarado et al., 1984; Alvarado et al., 1981), malfunction of TM phagocytosis (Buller et al., 1990)
evidence: This is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: Elevated IOP is associated with abnormal deposition of extracellular matrix (ECM).

evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Trabecular meshwork stem cells (TMSCs) have their special niche located at the anterior TM tissue beneath the Schwalbe's line.
